can: I can explain what the analysis found, show you the moments in the video, suggest gym exercises and show how to do them, and build a simple practice plan.

three_d.text: The video is one flat camera view, so anything towards or away from the camera is estimated, not measured. Angles are called projected for that reason, and I cannot give true 3D angles.

angles.text: Angles are read from the flat picture, so a limb pointing towards the camera looks shorter and its angle can be off. Treat them as projected estimates, not exact joint angles.

force.text: I cannot measure force, power or how hard you hit. I only see body positions and timing in the video.

muscles.text: I cannot see which muscles are working or how tired they are. I only see how your body moves in the picture.

shuttle.text: The shuttle is not tracked, so I cannot tell shot speed, shot type, placement, or whether it landed in. The advice uses player movement and timing only.

racket.text: I cannot see the racket face, grip or strings clearly enough to measure them. I follow the hitting hand instead.

body.text: I cannot measure heart rate, calories or anything inside the body. I only see movement in the video.

accuracy.text: Numbers come from one flat video, so they are estimates. Each one has a confidence word: fairly sure, somewhat sure or not very sure. Use them as practice guides, not exact measurements.

norms.text: The target ranges are general practice guides from coaching, not norms tested for your body or level. They were not checked against amateur players, so use them as a direction, not a pass mark.

speed.text: Speeds are read from the picture and the court lines, so they are rough. Small changes between clips may be noise.

doubles.text: The analysis follows two players, so it is built for singles. In a doubles game some numbers may be off.

medical.text: I cannot give medical advice or say whether something will prevent injury. For health questions, please ask a doctor or physiotherapist.

preview.text_preview: This is the fast preview, so the numbers are quick estimates and the full analysis can change them. Treat them as a first look.
preview.text_refined: This is the full analysis, but the numbers still come from one flat video, so treat them as estimates and practice guides, not exact measurements.

general.text: I only see body movement in one flat video. I cannot track the shuttle, the racket, your heart rate or true 3D angles, so angles are called projected and every number is an estimate with a confidence word. Targets are practice guides, not norms tested for you.
